 King Charles gives William extraordinary power as Harry spreads wings
 Prince William has proven he can carry the weight without complaint
 By 
 Shehzad Hameed 
 | 
 Published October 24, 2026 
 King Charles gives William extraordinary power as Harry spreads wings In a decisive shift in strategy after Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's UK return, the Palace is protecting its future and winning the PR war with bold and calculated moves from Prince William and Princess Kate.
 King Charles has seemingly handed his heir extraordinary new powers at the exact moment the Duke of Sussex is spreading his wings to secure his future.
 The future British monarch is no longer being prepared, indeed, he is being empowered as the King knows his time is about managing the transition, not holding on to everything.
 READ MORE: Prince William shares message for 'Traitors', reveals dream job 
 A senior royal source confirms: "The King is gradually transferring authority to William, giving him unprecedented control over the Crown Estate decisions, royal patronages and even the final say on who represents the monarchy in the future."
 "William has proven he can carry the weight without complaint, without drama. He stood by his father during his illness, he stood by Kate, he kept the monarchy steady when others walked away. That loyalty has been rewarded," the insider added.
 After his cancer diagnosis and amidst a changing modern landscape, King Charles views his reign as a bridge to the future, focusing on managing a smooth transition rather than attempting to hold onto a vast, lifelong legacy.
 Prince William's appearance on 'The Graham Norton Show' suggests he fully accepts the challenge to strengthen the monarchy and keep it alive with a modern touch.
 The future monarch's bold move has offered the royal family a major publicity opportunity amid renewed scrutiny surrounding Meghan Markle's estranged father, fueling speculation about whether the monarchy is gaining ground in its long-running public relations rivalry with the Sussexes.
 The show, which aired Friday, October 23, on BBC One , promoted his environmental initiative, the Earthshot Prize.
 William was introduced unexpectedly during the program after Norton began discussing the Earthshot Prize with the other guests.
 The discussion also explored lighter subjects, including William's longstanding support for Aston Villa and his enthusiasm for films directed by Christopher Nolan.
 It comes after Prince Harry's latest interview, where he spoke of his childhood ordeal, future plans and a renewed offer of reconciliation.
 Unlike the Duke of Sussex, William's relaxed appearance provided an opportunity to promote a cause that has become central to his public work.
 King Charles has openly praised Prince William's diplomacy and deliberately accelerated his involvement in strategic leadership, emphasising that the success of the monarchy depends on a strong relationship passed between generations.
 Sources say the King admires Harry's independence, but his focus is crystal clear — the Crown must be safe in William's hands.
 The King's and William's joint message to the world is loud and clear: The House of Windsor is not just surviving — indeed, it is preparing for the next 50 years, with Prince William at the very centre of it.
 While Harry flies higher on his own path, William is now flying the flag for the Crown itself.
